history of axillary hyperhidrosis
excessive sweating of the buttocks
most severe sweating at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum

shortlist.label: hyperhidrosis

shortlist.label: fabry disease

raw.rationale: The patient's history of axillary hyperhidrosis and current symptoms of excessive sweating of the buttocks, particularly at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, align with the characteristics of hyperhidrosis. The Minor starch-iodine test results further support this diagnosis by identifying areas of significant sweating.

rejected.label: eccrine nevus
rejected.why: Eccrine nevus is a rare condition that typically presents with localized hyperhidrosis, but the patient's symptoms and test results suggest a more generalized condition.

rejected.label: fabry disease
rejected.why: Fabry disease is a genetic disorder that can cause hyperhidrosis, but it is typically associated with other systemic symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: cholinergic urticaria
rejected.why: Cholinergic urticaria is a condition that causes hives and itching in response to heat or exercise, but it does not typically cause excessive sweating.

rejected.label: graves disease
rejected.why: Graves' disease is an autoimmune disorder that can cause hyperthyroidism, which may lead to excessive sweating, but the patient's symptoms and test results do not suggest thyroid dysfunction.
